issues: The checker's facts all hold against the full text of arXiv 2302.03025, Tables 5 and 6, Fig 7, Sec 6 and App C. The recommended bibtex (PMLR 202:6243-6267) matches the PMLR page. The current refs.bib entry lacks volume and pages. S5 support is stronger than the checker states: all 4 transformer seeds are sign plus exactly one 4d faithful irrep (standard-sign twice, standard twice), and 2/4 MLP seeds and the Fig 7 mode are sign plus standard. A5: the Galois 3d pair alone appears in 2/4 transformer seeds. The seed that adds 5d-a has test loss 0.195 and did not generalize; the other seed is {standard} only. Every A5 MLP seed adds the 4d standard irrep. So 'as observed' for A5 needs scoping to transformers, or attribution to the paper's own runs. The intro's 'a few irreps' is too broad for their cyclic and dihedral MLPs (9-15 key irreps), so scope it to non-abelian groups. Chughtai never tests S4. groups.tex mentions S4 only in the interference sentence, which is unattributed, but it should not imply Chughtai data. Chughtai uses ReLU plus AdamW (wd=1), not max-margin product nets, so 'consistent with' is the right strength. Optional: also cite Stander et al. (ICML 2024, coset account of the same S5/S6 networks) and Wu et al. (ICLR 2025, which unifies the irrep and coset accounts) so a reviewer who favors the coset reading is answered. Harness note: the session-wide WebSearch budget is exhausted (200/200), so verifiers can only fetch directly; this likely contributes to the slow verify stage.

extra_citations.why: Reverse-engineers S5/S6 one-hidden-layer MLPs as coset/subgroup circuits and contrasts this with Chughtai's irrep account. Cite it alongside Chughtai when saying group-composition networks use a few irreps.
An ICLR 2025 paper that unifies the Chughtai (irrep) and Stander (coset) explanations of group-operation networks. It is the current reference point for the empirical mechanism.
